newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- MARCH 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- MARCH 27.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--Excessive liquidity in the banking system yesterday led the Bank of Greece to reduce its intervention rate to 9.9 percent for deposits of over 300 billion drachmas. Although expected, the measure immediately resulted in the outflow of short-term capital of 350 million drachmas while the total outflows in the next few days is expected to come to one billion drachmas.

--Eurobank and Credit Lyonnais Greece yesterday announced an agreement for Eurobank's purchase of Credit Lyonnais' Greek network, expanding the Latsis Group-run Eurobank's presence in the domestic banking sector.
--The reserve price for the sale of Cretabank has been set at 30 billion drachmas, the government and Bank of Greece has decided.

--The Bank of Greece has signalled a change in its intervention tactics in an effort to more effectively control excessive liquidity. The move also signals a significant decrease in interest rates with the finance ministry announcing that the April 1 issue of zero coupons and Treasury bills will have slightly reduced rates ranging from 10.1 to 10.3 percent before tax.
--Five major retailers have resorted to the Council of State, Greece's highest administrative court, over the new trading hours schedule.
--The Bank of Cyprus yesterday posted profits of over 37.0 percent for 1996.

--Sources at the national economy and finance ministries have indicated that the fiscal deficit has fallen by half in the first three months of 1997, compared to the figure for the same period last year. The positive development is attributed to falling interest rates as a consequence of lower inflation and the release of 100 billion drachmas from the servicing of the public debt.
--Prime Minister Costas Simitis yesterday urged the transport ministry to be more effective at absorbing EU funds in the sector of transport and infrastructure, following his visit to the ministry.
--Greek shipping sees an increase in the trend to flee the Greek register if the government does not take immediate measures for the competitiveness of the Greek merchant marine.

--The finance ministry is delaying announcing any official extension of the deadline for submission of tax declarations, requested by tax services staff who claim that two million pensioners and wage-earners have yet to submit theirs.

--The government is reported to be considering the creation of a second national telecoms organisation, alongside OTE, in cooperation with the private sector, ahead of the imminent deregulation of the telecoms market.

--Sources say Development Minister Vasso Papandreou has already put together a working draft of a coordinating body to forge ahead with the government's "Balkan vision" of investment. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
